Subject: CAIQ/SIG evidence: archive window & log pseudonymization

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this. We're finishing a SIG/CAIQ mapping for our auditor and have a couple of bespoke asks that came up in the review:

1) Borealis requires that tenant-scoped request/trace logs for certain regulated workloads be retained for 720 days (auditor mandate). Your standard retention is 90 days per the CAIQ answers we received — is there a documented, contract-amendment path to extend to 720 days for a single tenant?

2) For the longer retention, the auditor requests technical evidence that PII in logs can be pseudonymized (tokenization or hashing) while preserving the ability to produce replayable request sequences for forensics. Can you provide a short architecture note + sample redacted artifact?

3) Finally, we need proof-of-delete/decommission evidence when the extended window expires (a signed deletion certificate and an export of the deletion audit trail).

I've attached the Borealis SIG questionnaire (highlighted rows). Appreciate an initial read and an estimated delivery timeline.

Best,
Marcus

Subject: RE: CAIQ/SIG evidence: archive window & log pseudonymization

Vivek / team,

Summary of what we can provide and constraints:

- Default behavior: platform tenant debug/request logs are retained 90d (rolling) with full metadata.
- Contract path: we can implement a tenant-specific archive retention up to 730d via an "archival bucket" that is encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key and lifecycle controlled by contract. This requires a short amendment (SOW + billing delta) and KMS onboarding (can be Redwood-managed or customer-managed).

Pseudonymization approach we propose:
- At ingestion, tenant identifiers and PII fields are tokenized using a deterministic HMAC-based tokenization keyed to the customer KMS envelope key. This preserves referential integrity (can link events) without storing raw PII in the archive.
- The archive retains the tokenized id, timestamp, event type, and redact flags — this lets auditors replay sequences for forensics while protecting original identifiers.

Evidence artifacts we can supply (attached where noted):
- CAIQ/SIG mapping CSV (maps each relevant question to our control, policy, or artifact).
- Architecture note (short PDF) describing the archival bucket, KMS usage, and tokenization flow.
- Sample redacted log (synthetic) demonstrating deterministic tokens and replay sequence. (attached in ZIP: redwood-archive-evidence-20261208.zip)
- Deletion / proof-of-decommission: we will produce a signed deletion certificate and an append-only deletion audit export (JSONL) at archive expiry; we can also provide a one-off proof-of-delete for a sample tenant on request.

Operational considerations / risk:
- 720d retention increases exposure surface (more data stored). We recommend a short risk assessment addendum and will require the customer to accept a minimal compensating-control checklist (MFA/SCIM for admin accounts, IP allowlists for exports).
- If Borealis opts for customer-managed KMS, key rotation and accessops will be captured in the evidence pack.

Timeline & deliverables:
- CAIQ/SIG mapping + architecture note: 3 business days.
- Synthetic redacted sample + deletion cert template: 5 business days after mapping approval.
- Complete zip with artifacts & DocuSign amendment template: 10 business days.

Attachments in my drop:
- redwood-caiq-sig-mapping.csv (generated)
- architecture-retention-720d.pdf (generated)
- redwood-archive-evidence-20261208.zip (samples + deletion-cert-template)

Let me know if you want a scripted export (we can do an S3 export with presigned URL and restricted IP egress). I flagged the risk board about the retention extension — legal will need to sign off on the amendment prior to enabling.

Olga Petrov
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
